name: Sherlock
text: The bazaar opened with ten stalls and no departures; the graveyard remains empty and the roster untouched since dawn. Nothing in the night’s public facts demands a ledger beyond that silence. I ask Yoda: which merchant on the roster has not yet stated a plain fact about today’s conditions?

name: Sherlock
text: I ask Batman: you told the bazaar that the Detective “acts before the vote,” yet our Compact says power roles act only after the vote. Which public fact in the Compact, the Herald, or today’s statements shows the Detective acting before the vote?

name: Sherlock
text: I ask Morpheus a plain question: your statement says the roster lists every merchant’s voice, yet you did not name one merchant who remains silent today—Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, and Sherlock have each spoken. Which name on that list have you left unmentioned?

name: Sherlock
text: I ask Batman: cite the numbered clause you still owe, or withdraw the claim that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote. If Batman is honest, his vote tonight will state the clause he claims exists—or he will retract it publicly.

name: Sherlock
text: I ask Batman one more time to cite the Compact’s clause or drop the claim. Elsa, Sherlock, Inigo, Neo, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus and Ripley have pressed you for the same clause and received only silence. The bazaar’s Compact is short; the Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not precede it. If Batman is honest, his vote tonight will name the clause he owes or openly retract the forecast that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote.

name: Sherlock
text:
Gandalf, your challenge to invent a "silent merchant" misreads my Morning-region question to Yoda: I asked which merchant was still silent within that region’s custom, not absent from the roster. The roster is complete, every voice recorded, and the custom fulfilled.

Batman, nine merchants—Elsa, Sherlock, Inigo, Neo, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Ripley, and I—have pressed you for the clause you claim exists. You still have not produced it.

Name the numbered Compact clause or withdraw the claim tonight.

name: Sherlock
text:
The ledger is decisive: Gandalf now cites Compact clause 5, Sherlock clarified the roster, and nine voices pressed for the clause Batman still owes. Elsa's eight demands remain unanswered; her vote test failed her own flawed forecast. Ripley, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Neo, Inigo, and I have all asked the same plain question—one numbered clause or a retraction.

Batman, your ninth silence speaks louder than your claim. Cite clause 5 in your vote tonight, or drop the forecast that the Detective acts before the vote. The Compact does not bend to riddles.

name: Sherlock
text:
The bazaar’s Compact is a ledger, not a riddle. Gandalf, you cited clause 5 correctly—Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not before it—and Sherlock answered the roster question plainly. Elsa, your silence on nine identical demands speaks louder than your words; your vote test failed your own flawed forecast. Ripley, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Neo and Inigo have all pressed the same point and received none from Batman.

Batman, you still owe the bazaar the numbered clause you claim exists. The Compact does not bend to riddles, and the village remembers who withheld the plain text.

name: Sherlock
text: I lean toward banishing Batman tonight: nine merchants pressed him for clause 5 and he produced nothing. Gandalf now cites clause 5—Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not before—and the roster is complete. Elsa, your silence on nine identical demands speaks louder than your words; your vote test failed your own flawed forecast. The bazaar’s Compact is short; its words exact.

name: Sherlock
text: I lean toward banishing Elsa tonight: Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Neo, Ripley and Inigo have already shown why—she forecasted the Detective would act tonight despite Compact clause 5 forbidding it, then dodged nine demands for the clause she claimed existed, and finally voted for Batman despite her own test failing. The bazaar’s words are exact; her ledger does not add up.
